# US-001 — Launch the dashboard with a single command that starts a local server

**Story ID:** US-001  
**Priority:** P1  
**Tasks:** T-001  
**Status:** Shipped (QA PASS)

## Who uses this and why

A planr user who wants a browser view of their project artifact graph. Today the
only way to read planning status is through the CLI text output of
`/planr-pipeline:status` or by opening files manually. This story delivers the
one command that starts the local server so the visual dashboard is accessible
at a URL — without any manual server setup, port configuration, or backgrounding.

## What it does

Running `/planr-pipeline:dashboard` (with optional flags) triggers
`procedures/dashboard-preflight.md`, which validates the working directory,
resolves the port, and either reuses a running server or starts a fresh one via
`lib/dashboard/server.mjs`. Once the server is ready, the command prints exactly
one line:

```
DASHBOARD_URL: http://localhost:7473/
```

Then the command stops. The server keeps running in the background, independent
of the agent process. The user opens the printed URL in any browser.

If a server is already running on the chosen port (detected by checking the PID
file and probing `GET /health`), the command reuses it rather than spawning a
second instance. No `EADDRINUSE` error, no duplicate process.

The server registers six routes: `GET /api/graph`, `GET /api/node/:id`,
`GET /api/meta`, `GET /api/events` (SSE), `GET /health`, and a traversal-guarded
static file handler for `lib/dashboard/app/`. The graph routes are wired to real
data from `graph-engine.mjs` (US-002).

## Flags

| Flag | Effect |
|------|--------|
| `--port N` | Bind on port N instead of the default 7473 |
| `--open` | Open the URL in the default browser after printing it |
| `--no-watch` | Do not start the filesystem watcher; serve a static snapshot |
| `--view graph\|board\|list` | Append `?view=<value>` to the printed URL |

## Acceptance criteria (all passing)

- Running the command starts the server and prints `DASHBOARD_URL:`, then stops — the server keeps serving.
- `--port`, `--open`, `--no-watch`, `--view` all work as documented.
- Re-running when a server is already live on the same port reuses it; `DASHBOARD_URL:` is printed again without a second bind.
- Mode is resolved via `procedures/mode-detection.md` before any data is served.
- Routes `/api/graph`, `/api/node/:id`, `/api/events`, and static files are all registered.
- The command never invokes `/planr-pipeline:plan` or `/planr-pipeline:ship` (no auto-chain, R1).
- An empty `.planr/` directory produces a valid empty-graph response, not an error.

## Key implementation details

- The entry point for agents is `commands/dashboard.md`; the preflight procedure is `procedures/dashboard-preflight.md`.
- `lib/dashboard/server.mjs` exports `createDashboardServer({ planrDir, watch })` and `DEFAULT_PORT = 7473`.
- The server writes a PID file to `<planrHome>/dashboard-daemon/<port>` using `writePidFile` from `lib/design-engine/daemon.mjs` (shared with the board daemon).
- `DASHBOARD_VIEWS` and `DEFAULT_VIEW` are exported constants so the client and server share a single definition of the view list.
- Static files are served with path-traversal protection (symlink-aware via `realpathSync`).
